rca of the issue: E1 root cause: analyze_preview_task previously set analysis_status='ready' first, THEN scheduled the R2 flush. Between those two operations there was a millisecond-scale window where /api/reports/{id}/status returned analysis_status=ready with video_url pointing to the LOCAL /api/uploads/<id>.mp4. The frontend, on seeing ready, started the <video> element. Meanwhile _flush_preview_artifacts_to_r2 uploaded the file to R2 and DELETED the local copy. The <video> element then GETs the local URL and receives 404. Fix: flush FIRST (sets video_url_override to the R2 URL), THEN flip status=ready — so by the time the frontend sees ready, the URL it renders is always the R2 URL. E2 root cause: no wall-clock timeout on the entire preview pipeline. Even with the 480s Gemini timeout from iter49, other steps (ffmpeg transcoding, content-gate Gemini call, preview Gemini call, R2 upload) could theoretically each stall for minutes. Worst case observed by user = 20 min stuck on step=2 (ffmpeg + content-gate). Fix: wrap the ENTIRE pipeline in asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=900). On timeout, mark failed + refund the upload eligibility (so the user isn't billed for a hung request). E3 root cause: legacy 'Cooking' verbiage from the marketing-focused MVP era conflicted with the current professional-scout tone. Users reading 'Step 2 of 5 · Cooking' during a stuck upload thought the app was broken/confused. Fix: rename to 'Analyzing' and align STAGE_LABELS map with the actual backend step semantics so users see meaningful progress descriptions.
